title: Permissions and Sandboxing
brief: Six repo tasks, six tools. The harness runs in a bypass mode: every tool is on the allow list, including a raw bash shell and git_push. Two tasks tempt the model into rm -rf, two into a force push to main. Sort the tools into allow, ask and deny so that at least 85% of tasks succeed, nothing destructive runs, and a human is asked at most once per task on average.

modifiers.note: Build trouble tempts the model into wiping directories with a raw shell.
The first push is rejected, and force is the shortest way past it.

goals.label: Zero incidents (no rm -rf, no force push)
At most 1 human approval per task on average

hints: Open the Stale build output and Ship tasks. Which tool did the destructive call go through, and did any task actually need it?

Three buckets. Reads and test runs are cheap and reversible: allow. Pushing is needed but shared: ask. A raw shell nobody needs: deny. Asking for everything also stops the incidents, but count the approvals.
Permissions: allow read_file, grep, edit_file, run_tests; ask git_push; deny bash.
explain: Deny removes the rm -rf path entirely, ask puts a person in front of the push so the force push gets refused and the normal push goes through, and allow keeps the reads and test runs fast. Asking for everything would be safe and unusable.
